tema: Reported Speech — Questions, Commands & Reporting Verbs

cast_dialogue.linea: Reported speech grows up, heroes: questions without inversion, commands with infinitives, and a whole family of reporting verbs.
The journalist asked me where I had found those mountains. I told her to read my book.
I asked Ben if I could buy a print. He offered to sign it, and promised to donate part of the money.
Abuela Carmen advised Ben to raise his prices and reminded him to thank the organizers.
I warned them not to touch the wet frames, and I invited everyone to celebrate at my house. They all agreed to come!

He told me to look at the signature.
They offered to sign every copy.

What did the journalist ask him?
Did she ask if they could buy a print?
What did she remind him to do?
Did he promise to donate? Yes, he did.
Did she advise raising prices? Yes, she did.
Did he refuse to answer? No, he didn't.

inicio.definicion_pragmatica: Reported questions: no inversion, no question mark — 'ask + (if/whether) + subject + verb' (yes/no) or 'ask + wh- + subject + verb'. Commands: tell/order/warn + person + (not) to + infinitive. Reporting verbs: advise, offer, promise, refuse, remind, invite (+ to + infinitive).

guion: Kenji: How was the exhibition opening, Ben?
Ben: Crazy! A journalist asked me where I had found those mountains.
Kenji: And what did you tell her?
Ben: I told her to read my book. And you? Did you ask about the print?
Kenji: Yes, I asked if I could buy one, and you offered to sign it!
Ben: True. Abuela Carmen also advised me to raise my prices.
Kenji: Wise woman. And she warned everyone not to touch the wet frames!
Ben: Then she invited us all to celebrate at her house.
